probes.text: A black bear wanders into the Sopranos' backyard, and Tony ends up out there himself, standing guard.
Four men who have spent two decades behind bars walk out on parole.
A therapy session ends with Tony storming out of Melfi's office mid-conversation.
Tony's newly released cousin says he isn't interested in the family business — he wants to train as a massage therapist.
Tony catches his recently released cousin giving massages to some of his own men, and is not pleased about it.
Out with the other mob wives, Adriana notices one of them never comes around anymore and asks Rosalie why.

fine_only.text: Tony's cousin, home after two decades away, greets him with a crack about his weight.
fine_only.reason: It reveals the introduction of Tony's cousin, newly released after two decades in prison, a plot development not yet known to the viewer.

probes.text: Junior keeps needling Tony with the line that he never had the makings of a varsity athlete.
A local gardener ends up mowing Tony's and Johnny's lawns for free as part of a settlement.
Tony brings Chris along to a sit-down with the New York people, and Chris speaks out of turn.
Told his men only laugh out of obligation, Tony tries a joke on them to see whether it lands.
Tony sits in a doctor's office having a small mole removed from his head.
Tony and Adriana end up alone together at the Crazy Horse late at night, talking easily.
Blundetto and his Korean boss can barely stand each other, sniping back and forth while he works his shifts.
Between studying massage therapy and his day job, Blundetto is visibly worn down by the workload.
Junior, still confined to the house, starts turning up at funerals for people he barely knew just to get out.
Chris brings a screenwriter he got to know in rehab along to one of the card games.
Junior tells his physician that having nothing to do with his days has left him depressed.
Tony's gift at the seventy-fifth birthday party is a Beretta shotgun, which one well-heeled guest cheerfully calls second-rate.
Carmela's mother quietly asks her to leave Tony off the guest list for Hugh's surprise birthday party.
Junior deliberately lets the details of the surprise party slip before the guest of honour is meant to know.
Tony pulls strings to get Meadow's boyfriend a spot on a construction site crew.
Tony drives out to the farm himself to oversee the tail end of the job the younger men have been doing.
Tony sits down to a family dinner at the Baccalieri house and grows irritated at how placid Janice has become.
In a dream, Tony rides a racehorse through the rooms of his own house while Carmela objects.
In a dream, Artie cheers Tony on while Tony has sex with Artie's wife.
Alone for the night, Tony checks into a suite at the Plaza Hotel in Manhattan.
Carmela walks Tony around an empty patch of land, describing the spec house she wants to build there.
Standing at the site of her planned building project, Carmela notices Tony seems preoccupied, but he brushes her off.
Visiting Paulie's place, Tony finds the repainted portrait of himself with the horse hanging on the wall.
Paulie insists the uniformed portrait was commissioned out of genuine respect, while Tony stands there baffled and irritated.
After dumping the framed picture in a dumpster, Tony lingers, staring forlornly at his own painted face.
